title: Motion Values passed via SVG style tag not updating on style
body:
**1. Describe the bug**
If you check the `vue/hold-to-confirm` example in the Motion Examples repo, we have added `opacity: circleOpacity`. This motion value does get applied to style on mount but doesn't seem to update when the motion value changes. Because of a pre-existing bug in the renderSVG function it does get updated on the attribute though.
author: mattgperry

comments.body: @mattgperry  I think i should remove it from the style attribute and handle it like motion/react does.

title: Pug syntax in template
body:
It seems impossible use motion.div in template with pug syntax. I have tried various combinations but without success.
Can you show me the right way of doing this, or implement this feature in the future?
Thanks!
author: emptyfortress

comments.body:
hi! @emptyfortress  Since .div gets compiled to a class prop, you can work around this by doing:
```
<script setup>
const Div = motion.div
</script>

<template lang="pug">
  Div()
</template>
```
Thank you for such a quick response! It works like a charm.

title: Adding v-slot for ReorderItem
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When using ReorderItem, I just want to set a cursor-grabbing when it is grabbed, but I need to put a variable in the template and then compare it to the value of the ReorderItem to apply it.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be great if the ReorderItem component exposed a "dragged" v-slot, so I can use it directly in the template.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Adding an `id` in the script, populated at the `@drag-start` to compare with the `ReorderItem`.
author: Ericlm

comments.body: That makes sense! I'll consider adding it.

title: `FeatureManager` improvement
body:
At this moment `FeatureManager` enables all features even if they aren't used by `Motion`. It leads to overhead and unwanted side effects. Most noticeable one is `PressGesture` feature uses `press` which sets `tabindex` to 0.

There is `isActive` method in most of the features, but as i can see `FeatureManager` ignores it. Would be nice to push this idea further.
author: zumm

comments.body: Not a top priority right now, but I'll handle this when adding LazyMotion support for smaller bundle sizes in the future.

title: fix(docs): Correct useInView docs ,simplify build and add image to readme for better branding
body:
# Improve Documentation and Add Logo

This pull request addresses several documentation issues and enhances the README with a logo.

**Key Changes:**

* **`CONTRIBUTING.md`:** Added instructions on how to build the documentation locally.
* **`README.md`:**
    * Added the Motion-Vue logo with the text "Motion-Vue". 
* **`docs/useInView`:** Corrected the documentation for the `useInView` hook. It now accurately states that the hook returns a *ref to a boolean*. `saying it returns a boolean could be confusing`
* **Documentation Build:** Modified the documentation build process to no longer require `execa`.

**Motivation:**

These changes aim to improve the overall developer experience by:

* Making the contribution process smoother.
* Enhancing the README with a visual element.
* Ensuring the accuracy of the documentation.
* Simplifying the documentation build process.

**Testing:**

* Verified that the documentation builds locally without errors.
* Confirmed the correct behavior of the `useInView` hook.
* Checked the display of the logo in the README.
author: ketsebaoteth

title: fix(motion): Use rimraf for cross-platform dist directory cleanup and add CONTRIBUTING readme
body:
fix(motion): Replace `rm -rf` with `rimraf` for cross-platform compatibility and add CONTRIBUTING.md for setup guide

The build script now uses `rimraf` to remove the `dist` directory, ensuring compatibility on non-Unix based systems where `rm -rf` may not be available or behave as expected.

I also added a CONTRIBUTING.md file for a guide on how to build this repo and run it locally.
author: ketsebaoteth
